title: Accelerated Development of Rod Photoreceptors in Retinal Organoids
author: Kelley, Chen, et al.

steps.title: Coat plates with hESC‑qualified Matrigel
steps.instruction: Prepare Matrigel coating for 6‑well plates using hESC‑qualified Matrigel.

substeps.instruction: Thaw a bottle of Matrigel in a covered Styrofoam box filled with ice; keep the box at 4 °C overnight (≥12 h). Freeze 1.5 mL tubes and 1 mL pipette tips at –20 °C.
Place the frozen tubes and the Matrigel bottle on ice in the Styrofoam container.
Gently invert the Matrigel bottle until the suspension is homogeneous.
On ice, quickly aliquot 240 µL of Matrigel (9.5 mg/mL) into each chilled 1.5 mL tube using chilled pipette tips.
Store the aliquots at –80 °C.
Add one 240 µL aliquot to 25 mL cold DMEM:F12 on ice; mix well.
Dispense 1 mL of the diluted Matrigel into each well of four 6‑well tissue‑culture plates using pre‑chilled pipette tips.
Wrap each plate individually with parafilm and cover all plates with aluminum foil to protect from light.
Store the coated plates at 4 °C for up to 2 weeks.

steps.title: Coat dishes with growth‑factor‑reduced Matrigel
steps.instruction: Prepare Matrigel coating for 60 mm dishes using growth‑factor‑reduced Matrigel, adjusting volume for lot concentration.

substeps.instruction: Note: Matrigel concentration may vary by lot; adjust aliquot volume according to the concentration listed on Corning Life Science’s certificate download page.
Thaw a bottle of Matrigel in a covered Styrofoam box filled with ice; keep the box at 4 °C overnight (≥12 h). Freeze 1.5 mL tubes and 1 mL pipette tips at –20 °C.
Place the frozen tubes and the Matrigel bottle on ice in the Styrofoam container.
Gently invert the Matrigel bottle a few times until the suspension is homogeneous.
On ice, quickly aliquot 240 µL of Matrigel into each chilled 1.5 mL tube using chilled pipette tips.
Store the aliquots at –80 °C.
Add one 240 µL aliquot to 18 mL cold DMEM:F12 on ice; mix well.
Dispense 3 mL of the diluted Matrigel into each of six 60 mm tissue‑culture dishes using pre‑chilled pipette tips.
Wrap each dish individually with parafilm and cover all dishes with aluminum foil to protect from light.
Store the coated dishes at 4 °C for up to 2 weeks.

steps.title: Apply polyHEMA coating to dishes
steps.instruction: Prepare and apply a polyHEMA coating to non‑treated petri dishes.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a 2 mg/mL solution of poly‑2‑hydroxyethyl methacrylate (polyHEMA) in 95 % ethanol; incubate at 65 °C until fully dissolved. Store the stock at 20‑22 °C.
Rinse non‑treated 60 mm and 100 mm petri dishes with the polyHEMA solution; return any unused solution to the stock.
Sterilize the rinsed dishes overnight (≥12 h) under UV light in the biosafety cabinet.
Wrap each sterilized dish individually with parafilm and store at 22‑25 °C until use.
